narration: For ordinary Filipinos, the most noticeable economic effects may involve prices, employment, and household spending. If political uncertainty contributes to a weaker peso, imported goods and materials could become more expensive in local currency. This may affect products such as fuel, medicines, electronics, and imported ingredients used by local manufacturers. Businesses facing higher costs may pass some of those increases on to consumers. At the same time, uncertainty about business activity can influence hiring decisions and household income. Families may respond by reducing nonessential purchases or setting aside more money for essential expenses. However, inflation and the cost of living are influenced by many factors, including supply conditions, energy prices, weather, transportation costs, and global markets. It would be misleading to blame changes in household expenses on an impeachment trial without evidence showing a direct economic connection. Yet the economic story is not entirely negative. A credible accountability process may also offer longer-term benefits.
